content.thinking:
I'm settling on a mechanism, and the dose data looks roughly linear. Comparing the two doses at matched time points, the ratio sits near 4 at most times, drifting slightly from it early on.

I'm working out the elimination rate from the terminal decline, which comes out near 0.1 per hour, about a 7-hour half-life. Then I'm estimating the absorption rate constant from the early peak, roughly 1 per hour, to set up a one-compartment oral model.

The steady-state scaling still holds, so I'm now converting the fitted coefficient back into a volume: about 0.019 per mg of F/V, which puts V on the order of the dose-normalized amplitude. I'll check the peak against the one-compartment curve next, since the difference-of-exponentials form needs its own correction factor.

I'm checking the absorption rate by comparing the predicted curve against observed points at 0.25, 1, and 2 hours. The model underpredicts the early values, so I'm testing a higher absorption constant of about 1.5 per hour and keeping the tail fit fixed by rescaling the coefficient.

I'm testing whether an absorption constant of about 1.3 per hour fits the early points better, and checking the predicted values at 0.5, 1, and 2 hours against the observed curve.

I'm checking the amplitude at the 200 mg dose using the same scaling and rate constants, to see whether the model stays consistent across both doses.

I'm estimating the volume from the scaled coefficient, taking F as 1 for now, which gives about 52 L. With the elimination rate near 0.1 per hour, that puts clearance around 5.2 L/h, and I'm settling on an absorption rate of 1.3 per hour. I'm treating these as apparent values, with moderate confidence.
